content:
**Athens** is a location in *Fallout 76*, introduced in the *Burning Springs* update.

Athens was originally settled in 1797 and founded alongside Hocking University in 1804. [2] [3] In 1874, the Athens Lunatic Asylum was constructed, and subsequently damaged beyond repair during the Storm of 2048, with the site coming under the management of the Athens Historical Society after its destruction. [4] In 1974, Athens celebrated its first annual Halloween celebration. [5] Abraxodyne Chemical operated an office in the city, located on Richland Avenue, across from Hocking University. An executive of the company resided in an apartment located on Washington Street in central Athens. The Pallas Cinema on College Street was showing several films in late October including *Night of the Fish Men's Revenge*, *Honk Honk Stab Stab*, and *Love Sets Sail!* Hocking University possessed a football team known as the Hogs, and an engineering department where Professor Franklin Metter taught. [6] [7] 

The day of the Great War, Athens did not directly witness the nuclear attack, but rather heard about it secondhand. [8] The city was placed under martial law by the Ohio National Guard lead by Captain Richard Murphy after its mayor perished an hour into the bombardment of a heart attack, with the chief of police missing, presumed dead. Murphy attempted to make contact with Columbus and Cleveland, to no avail. [9] As civilian disaster relief efforts were underway at the church, a train carrying Abraxodyne Chemical waste derailed on the edge of town, spilling its contents into the environment and contaminating the town's groundwater. [8] On October 25th, a number of seismic events struck the town, believed by Captain Murphy to have been caused by aftershocks of the nuclear exchange. The resulting event severely damaged the region, causing large shifts in the terrain and severely damaging the town's infrastructure, including water pipes, exacerbating the issues caused by the contaminated groundwater. The National Guard began constructing makeshift walkways to traverse the city. [10] 

In the following weeks, the situation in Athens worsened, with heavy rationing of water due to the contamination. Citizens resorted to stealing water from their neighbors to survive. [11] Captain Murphy dispatched scouts to Cleveland and Columbus to attempt to make contact, none of whom returned. On November 2nd, scouts sent to survey the local area returned and reported on the contamination of the region, now known as Burning Springs, by chemicals originating from Abraxodyne. Captain Murphy ordered the closure of Athens' borders, believing that with the city's limited resources they could not care for any potential refugees. [12] A water purifier was constructed by students of Hocking University, but while national guardsmen were rationing the water, a riot broke out which resulted in the deaths of 3 civilians, Private Kupowski, and the destruction of the purifier. [13] 

As time passed, members of the community began experiencing ghoulification, beginning with a mailman who had entered the city prior to the closure. [14] National Guard Medical Officer Edwin Greer identified the condition as an unknown disease, and it was feared that ghoulified individuals would upset the tenuous public order. On December 8th, Captain Murphy ordered that any feral individuals be killed and disposed of via burn pits located throughout the city, such as on Congress Street. Living individuals showing signs of ghoulificiation were to be exiled from the city. [15] [16] Feral Ghouls began congregating around the city, causing the national guardsmen stationed there to begin preparing for an attack. [17] 

By December 21st, order had completely broken down within Athens. Much of the civilian population, such as Professor Franklin Metter, had fled into the wasteland, with those remaining ghoulifying. Members of the Hocking University Football team, such Frank "4-eyes" Rogers and Steve departed into the wasteland, becoming a gang of Raiders. [18] [19] Several national guardsmen had feralized, and been burned, with Medical Officer Greer taking the key to the armory and departing east, traveling along the rail lines. Captain Murphy remained in the Athens armory to defend it, and prevent anyone from acquiring the armaments stored there. [20] [21] 

By 2105 Athens is abandoned, with a reputation as a cursed city, from which people do not return. [1] [22] It is inhabited only by Feral Ghouls, the Protectrons utilized by the National Guard to maintain order, Bodhi, and a surviving executive of the Abraxodyne Chemical company. Signs surround the town warning of its danger, and citizens of Highway Town remark on the location, stating its name should be "Ambush". The Rust King on his travels visited Athens, bringing with him a priest whom he requested spread his scripture to the world so that like minded outsiders would come join The Rust Kingdom. [23] A scavenging team from Highway Town lead by Schmidt entered the city, finding little resistance and believed the rumors about the city to be exaggerated. However while camping on the Hocking University grounds the group was overwhelmed by Feral Ghouls and killed. [1] 

Athens appears in *Fallout 76*.
